claims.text: The initial almost-equiatomic FeCoNi-based alloy has an fcc structure.
The initial almost-equiatomic FeCoNi-based alloy has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
A controlled thermal treatment can trigger in situ formation of nanoscale secondary precipitates in an FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
The precipitation treatment can retain the alloy's overall high-entropy character.
The treatment will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale ordered intermetallic precipitates in an fcc matrix.
The precipitates are likely to be B2-type.
Dispersed nanoscale intermetallic precipitates act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Domain-wall pinning by the precipitates increases the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
The increased barrier to domain-wall motion raises coercivity.
Precipitation produces magnetic inhomogeneity in the alloy.
Precipitation-treated FeCoNi will have noticeably higher coercivity than the FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives.
The FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives are soft ferromagnets with low coercive fields.
A significant coercivity enhancement requires the precipitates to be uniformly dispersed and stable.
Precipitate coarsening may eliminate or reduce the proposed coercivity enhancement.
Extensive diffusion during heat treatment can cause precipitate coarsening, excessive grain growth, or phase separation.
Formation of a fully multiphase structure with reduced configurational entropy may make the proposed mechanism ineffective.

contradictions.description: The comparison baseline is inconsistent: the predicted outcome names FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, the baseline permits either unmodified FeCoNi or those derivatives, and the experiment instead uses an untreated or standard-processed FeCoNi-based sample.

The intervention explicitly creates a secondary precipitate phase, while other fields seek to preserve a high-entropy single-phase structure or avoid a fully multiphase state. The permissible amount of phase separation is not defined, leaving the intended phase-state criterion internally ambiguous.
